chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Simāʿah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the beetle that falls into water: may wudu (ablution) be performed from it? He said: “Yes, there is no harm in it.” I said: And the scorpion? He said: “Pour it out.”

Also indicating this is what the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abī Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, in a long hadith, who said:
He was asked about the beetle, the fly, the locust, the ant, and whatever resembles that, dying in the well, oil, ghee, and the like. He said: “Everything that has no blood, there is no harm in it.”

key_terms.أَرِقْهُ: pour it out; discard the liquid
key_terms.الزَّيْتِ: oil mentioned among liquids affected by such cases
key_terms.السَّمْنِ: ghee mentioned alongside oil and well water
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well in which such creatures may die
key_terms.الْخُنْفَسَاءِ: the beetle mentioned as falling into water or dying in liquids
key_terms.الْعَقْرَبُ: the scorpion, concerning which the liquid is ordered to be poured out
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water from which wudu (ablution) may be performed
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood; the ruling is tied to whether the creature has blood

ai.seo_question: Does water remain usable for wudu (ablution) if a beetle or similar insect falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding water and similar substances in which certain small creatures fall or die. It indicates that creatures without flowing blood do not render such liquids problematic, while the scorpion is treated differently in the first report.
